name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
charge: Oppressing Israel; drowning their sons; refusing the Lord's command
summary: The king who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel, ordered their male infants thrown into the river, and when Moses came in the Lord's name answered, Who is the Lord? He hardened his heart through ten plagues and drowned in the sea he pursued Israel into.
offense: The policy was deliberate and it is quoted: come on, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies (Exodus 1:10). What followed was forced labour with rigour, and lives made bitter with hard bondage, in morter and in brick and in all manner of service in the field (Exodus 1:13-14), and when the affliction only increased them he moved to infanticide by decree, every son that is born ye shall cast into the river (Exodus 1:22). To the Lord's command he answered, Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go (Exodus 5:2). Then the pattern that gives him his sentence: each time a plague lifted he hardened his heart and would not let the people go, and he broke his word repeatedly with the evidence in front of him. Paul reads the outcome as appointed, for the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth (Romans 9:17).
judgment: Ten plagues came upon the country, and they were not random: against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment, I am the Lord (Exodus 12:12), and the record confirms it was carried out, upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments (Numbers 33:4). Each stroke shamed a thing Egypt worshipped, the river, the beasts, the light, and the last of them took the firstborn of every house from the throne to the dungeon, and there was not a house where there was not one dead (Exodus 12:29-30). He let them go and pursued them, and the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them (Exodus 14:27-28). Wisdom's summary is that a strange death found them, and that the element of the sea, which had let Israel pass, drowned the pursuers (Wisdom of Solomon 19:1-5).

verses.text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.
And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:

Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.
Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.
But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour:
And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
And Pharaoh said, Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go.
And he hardened Pharaoh’s heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had spoken unto Moses.

And it came to pass, that at midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.
And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.
For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.
As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do;
How that having given them leave to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them.
For whilst they were yet mourning and making lamentation at the graves of the dead, they added another foolish device, and pursued them as fugitives, whom they had intreated to be gone.

For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them unto this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfil the punishment which was wanting to their torments:
And that thy people might pass a wonderful way: but they might find a strange death.

And when they had determined to slay the babes of the saints, one child being cast forth, and saved, to reprove them, thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water.

text.text: For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments.

lawDetails.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.

entries.commentary: All the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls, for Joseph was in Egypt already; and Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty, and the land was filled with them. Israel had those babies; the nation did not cast away its children, and the increase was the blessing.

Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph: this is not merely one king but a new kingdom arising, the eighteenth dynasty. Come on, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply and join our enemies: the same wise dealing works on Israel in America today, through movements set up to redirect the people, through Planned Parenthood, and through the prison industrial complex; but the enemy did not count on Christ returning, restoring the nation, and bringing us back to the commandments of God. They set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses; but the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. The Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour, and made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter and in brick and in all manner of service in the field.

The king of Egypt commanded the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill every son born upon the stools and save the daughters alive; but the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. The midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them; the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations. Because the midwives feared God, God dealt well with them and made them houses; the Most High blessed the women who saved the children of Israel alive, and the people multiplied and waxed very mighty.
Pharaoh then charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive. ---

Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover. Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. The Lord had already said He would harden Pharaoh's heart.

They said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.

The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them.

Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters the same day: ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick; let them go and gather straw for themselves; and the tale of the bricks ye shall lay upon them, ye shall not diminish ought thereof. For they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God. Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words. The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High. The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.

The people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw, and the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw. Fewer resources, the same production and the same deadline: the pattern of oppression has not changed in this captivity. The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. Israelites were set as officers over their own people, so that the anger of the oppressed lands on their own brother, the supervisor they can see, instead of on the power above him; it has always been an agenda, and it is the same one today. This place is the same house of bondage in the spirit: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, and the afflictions Egypt laid on Israel are the same tactics laid on Israel here.

The officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now. The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt.

They met Moses and Aaron and said, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us. The people blamed the deliverers for the increase of affliction. It is the same spirit that meets the truth today, preferring quiet assimilation to deliverance; the enemy turns up the pressure precisely because the truth is being spoken.

Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all. Affliction can increase when the truth first goes forth, and the deliverer himself can be shaken by it. Walk in wisdom under that pressure and hold the tongue where wisdom requires, without letting go of the work. Have the faith to see ahead. The work of the Lord grows from a handful over many years because He sees the faith of those who endure, though at the time they cannot yet see what it will become. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips. This is why you do not move in a spirit of speaking against your leadership. Airing your complaints in front of everybody instead of bringing them in order only shows what type of spirit you are moving in; it is completely out of order.

It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent. The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and their rods became serpents; but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

All the waters of Egypt were turned to blood, in the streams, the rivers, the ponds, the pools, and in vessels of wood and vessels of stone; the fish died and the river stank. With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters. The magicians did so with their enchantments, but they could only copy the plague; they could not turn the water back clear. Seven days were fulfilled after the Lord had smitten the river. Many Egyptologists claim this never happened, because to admit it happened is to admit that the idols they claim to be gods and goddesses were powerless before our God, and that those idols do not exist at all.

A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle. The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead; and his heart was hardened. Picture what was taking place in the land: flies all over Egypt, but where Israel dwelt there were no flies; the water was blood, but where Israel dwelt the water was good; the cattle of Egypt died, but Israel's cattle lived. The plagues touched Pharaoh, his servants, and the Egyptians only; they did not touch the Israelites at all, because this was the Lord redeeming the Israelites. The Egyptians could not pray to their idols to help them, because the Lord was mocking them, showing them that Hathor does not exist, Sobek does not exist, Heqet does not exist, and Beelzebub does not exist.

Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt. The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty.

Some mock and ask, What type of God says let my people go and then keeps hardening Pharaoh's heart so he will not let them go? That is exactly the God we serve, and the Lord tells you Himself why He did it: for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth. The same thing is happening now, right here in this captivity. The powers of Babylon know what is being taught, yet the Lord hardens their hearts so that they keep passing laws and pressing against His people, so that the Most High can show His power again, just as He did in Egypt.

Before the hail the Lord gave warning: gather thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field, for upon every man and beast found in the field the hail shall come down, and they shall die. He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses; they began to recognize the God of heaven and earth, the God of the Israelites. He that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. Many in Egypt held certain idols in more favor than others, and these trusted that Nut, the idol goddess of the sky, would keep them safe.

This was no regular hail. There was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation; the fire ran along upon the ground. With this seventh plague the Most High was mocking Nut and Geb, the Egyptian idol gods of the sky and the earth, striking from the sky and burning along the ground they were supposed to rule. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. The Lord does not play; our God is a terrible God.

Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it. Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God.
The flax and the barley were smitten, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was bolled; but the wheat and the rie were not smitten, for they were not grown up.

When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. He still had the wheat and the rie in the ground, because they were not grown up yet, and that is part of why he went right back to hardening himself. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

This month shall be unto you the beginning of months, the first month of the year. The month is Abib, the month in which Israel came out of Egypt. Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon.

In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls. The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.

The whole assembly of the congregation of Israel was to kill the lamb in the evening, and take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses. The flesh was to be eaten that night, roast with fire, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs. That is the Passover menu in layman's terms: lamb roast with fire, unleavened bread, bitter herbs; no fried chicken, no birthday cake, no mashed potatoes and gravy, none of the thirteen herbs and spices.

Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water: do not boil it, but roast it with fire, the head with the legs and the purtenance thereof, and let nothing of it remain until the morning; what remains is burned with fire. It was to be eaten with loins girded, shoes on the feet, and staff in hand, in haste: it is the Lord's passover, and that very night Israel was leaving Egypt.

The Lord would pass through the land that night and smite all the firstborn of man and beast, and against all the gods of Egypt he would execute judgment. Each plague put an Egyptian god to shame: when he smote the land with darkness he showed that the sun god Ra is no god at all, for the God of heaven and earth blotted out the sun three days. Israel had to learn that those gods are nothing, because the nation was about to come out and serve the one true God. The blood was a token upon the houses: when I see the blood, I will pass over you. That is where the term Passover comes from; the houses with the blood on the doorposts were passed over from death while the firstborn of Egypt were slain.

This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away.

Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day the leaven is put out of the houses, and whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh, that soul shall be cut off from Israel. The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations; no manner of work is done in them save that which every man must eat, meaning the food may be cooked. The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys.

In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even. The Passover begins and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even; it is not difficult. Sin puts blinders on: when you hate your brother you are in darkness and cannot see what the scripture plainly says. Many fell away from the truth over this very point of the day beginning at evening. For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel.

The elders were to draw out a lamb for their families and kill the passover, take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts; the hyssop bush was used like a paintbrush to paint the blood of the lamb over the doorposts. None of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning: stay inside, for the Lord passes through to smite the Egyptians, and where he sees the blood he will pass over the door and will not suffer the destroyer to come in to smite you. The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.

This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. When the children ask, What mean ye by this service? the answer is, It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death.

Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead. The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone. The Egyptians were urgent upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, We be all dead men.

The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders. As Moses had said, they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent them what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians. They took everything.

The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name.

A mixed multitude went up also with them, and flocks and herds, even very much cattle. The mixed multitude that left with Israel were not to be among the children of Israel as rulers. The law sets the order: bondmen and bondmaids are to be of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among you; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children. But over the brethren, the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared any victual. The sojourning of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day, all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt. It is a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is the Passover night, which all the children of Israel are to observe in their generations.

This is the ordinance of the passover: no stranger eats of it. A bought servant may eat when he is circumcised; a foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof. When a stranger will keep the passover of the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and he shall be as one born in the land; one law is to the homeborn and to the stranger. It is eaten in one house, none of the flesh carried outside, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb, whose bones were not broken on the cross. Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

The Most High is not done with the Egyptians. He destroyed their firstborn and brought Israel out, but He kept one more judgment in store for that wicked nation, and He will do the same to the wicked nation that has done the same things to Israel today. The heart of Pharaoh and of his servants turned as soon as the people were gone: why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us? The oppressor does not release his slaves gladly.

At the first sight of the Egyptians marching, Israel lost all faith. The Lord had done miracle after miracle before their eyes and brought them out with an high hand, yet at the first sign of danger they said He brought them out to die. Our people have always been a rebellious people of little faith: a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians: that is the same word our people speak today. Why are you stirring up trouble, why tell us to come out of the ways of Babylon; let us alone to serve the slave master, because serving him feels easier than having faith in the Most High. The same spirit was in Israel in the days of Christ: if we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come. The fear of the oppressor outweighed belief in the miracles. In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord. The Egyptians whom ye have seen today, ye shall see them again no more for ever; that sounds like the same word that will stand over Babylon. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. The battle was never Israel's to win by strength.

The angel of God that went before the camp, the angel in the chariot whom we know to be Christ, removed and went behind them, standing between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. The pillar was a cloud and darkness to the Egyptians but gave light by night to Israel, so that the one came not near the other; Egypt could not see clearly where they were going. The Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night; Israel went through on dry ground, and the waters were a wall on the right hand and on the left.

In the morning watch the Lord troubled the host of the Egyptians and took off their chariot wheels, so that they said, Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord fighteth for them. Moses stretched out his hand and the sea returned in his strength. All that water that had stood up as a wall came down on the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen, and consumed them. All praises to the Most High for loving His children enough to save us by such a mighty salvation.

Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore and saw the great work of the Lord, and the people feared the Lord and believed the Lord and His servant Moses. The Lord who brought us out the first time with great signs and wonders will save Israel out of this captivity the same way; that is why the brothers and sisters must have faith in these last days, because a trial is the true test of faith. We have to accept that our salvation was their destruction. The Red Sea opened for Israel and closed on Egypt in the same hour; whoever hates that the Most High saves one nation by destroying the others will have to come to grips with it. Even the ground testified: where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream; grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
If a man strikes his servant and he dies at his hand, he shall be punished.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.
Cursing or blasphemy against God forbidden.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.

text.text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.
And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:

Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.
Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.
But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour:
And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
And Pharaoh said, Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go.
And he hardened Pharaoh’s heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had spoken unto Moses.

And it came to pass, that at midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.
And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.
For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.
As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do;
How that having given them leave to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them.
For whilst they were yet mourning and making lamentation at the graves of the dead, they added another foolish device, and pursued them as fugitives, whom they had intreated to be gone.

For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them unto this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfil the punishment which was wanting to their torments:
And that thy people might pass a wonderful way: but they might find a strange death.

And when they had determined to slay the babes of the saints, one child being cast forth, and saved, to reprove them, thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water.
